items.title: Data centers are paying about 4x what homebuilders pay for comparable land, finds Acres.com CEO Carter Malloy
items.description: At ResiDay 2026 in New York City on Friday, November 6, ResiClub spoke with Carter Malloy , CEO of Acres.com , to talk about a new competitor for land: AI data centers. Acres.com started as a land acquisition business. It closed about 150 deals across the country before turning its in-house tools into a land data platform. Its customers now include large builders such as Lennar, Toll Brothers, and Century Communities, as well as data center developers. One thing the platform does is track land purchases, including buys made through shell companies and outside attorneys, so users can see who is actually buying in a given market. Here's what that data shows, according to Malloy : Data centers aren't everywhere builders are. They're active in only about 10% of the markets where homebuilders operate. But where they're active, they pay far more. On average, data centers are paying about 4x what builders pay for comparable land. For powered land, the gap widens to 10x, 15x, even 20x. Malloy pointed to Central Ohio, where he said the premium is 10x or more across the whole region. The bigger problem is seller expectations. "The problem for us as builders is not, oh, I lost that one parcel," Malloy said. Landowners already had high asking prices, and when a data center moves into the area, they push prices even higher. Malloy called it "an acute problem, not a broad one." Builders don't need to bid on the same parcel as a data center to feel it. If a data center is going up nearby, land costs more, and homes are harder to sell when buyers know there will be a "24/7” noise down the street. Malloy said local governments are pushing back on data centers more and more. Acres' tracking counts more than 400 local data center moratoriums, and he said even that number is low. His bigger worry for builders is where that pushback goes next. Acres' data also shows moratoriums on residential development, multifamily housing, and subdivisions. Once a city council finds out it can stop one kind of development, Malloy said, it may be more willing to stop others. "That is a thing that we are all going to face, I believe, more in the coming year than we have yet." On technology, Malloy said the most innovative builders are doing much more than chatting with ChatGPT. Some, like Lennar and Toll Brothers, have set up in-house development teams that build their own AI tools and connect them to their CRM and ERP systems. Put one person in charge of evaluating AI tools. There are a lot more vendors now. Put a formal AI governance policy in writing, and ask vendors for zero data retention (ZDR) agreements. These are legal promises that your data won't be stored or used to train models.

items.title: Omaha’s Industrial Market Rewards an Integrated Approach
items.description: Omaha’s Industrial Market Rewards an Integrated Approach by Kristin Harlow November 26, 2026 November 26, 2026 1 By Chris Trosper, Opus Omaha can look deceptively simple from a development perspective. Land appears plentiful, industrial vacancy remains tight and the metro continues to attract companies looking for modern space. But the amount of land that is actually ready for development is considerably smaller than a map might suggest. The role of infrastructure Omaha’s approach to infrastructure helps explain why. Sanitary and improvement districts, or SIDs, have helped extend roads, water, sewer and other infrastructure into developing areas for decades. They also help explain why land that is available is not necessarily ready for development. Chris Trosper, Opus Turning available land into a development-ready site can require significant time and capital, particularly when a SID and new infrastructure are involved. The process can take nine months to a year, and the commitment becomes even more substantial when a developer is contemplating a large tract that will be built out in phases over many years. Even experienced, well-capitalized developers have to be selective about when that investment makes sense. For those that move forward, that upfront investment is reflected in the value of the development-ready land. A development-ready parcel may carry a premium over nearby undeveloped property because the time, cost and uncertainty involved in preparing the site have already been addressed. The SID process therefore helps moderate the pace of development in Omaha. The metro has room to grow, but converting raw land into industrial inventory takes time, which can help keep new supply from getting too far ahead of demand. Current market conditions bring that dynamic into sharper focus. Industrial vacancy remained below 3 percent during the first half of 2026, leaving fewer options for users with requirements that cannot easily be accommodated in existing buildings. Yet tight vacancy does not mean every available site should become a speculative industrial project. Once a viable site is available, the more consequential question is what kind of development best responds to demand in that location. Different demand, solutions Two Opus projects underway in the same northwest Omaha industrial park illustrate how different the answer can be. Rainwood Industrial is a 272,000-square-foot speculative industrial building designed to accommodate a broad range of warehouse and distribution users. The other project is a 65,000-square-foot build-to-suit headquarters and operations facility for Viking Industrial Painting. They are advancing in the same submarket and responding to the same broader market conditions, but the design and development strategies are fundamentally different. For the speculative building, flexibility is central to managing the uncertainty inherent in developing without a committed tenant. The building can accommodate as many as six users, while its loading configuration can expand as tenant needs become known. Those decisions preserve optionality without attempting to anticipate every possible requirement. An integrated design-build approach allows that flexibility to be considered from the outset. Development, design, engineering and construction teams can weigh marketability alongside constructability, cost and schedule as the building takes shape. Instead of designing the building first and pricing it later, the team can continually test decisions against both the market and the economics of the project. The objective is not to create a building for every possible user. It is to make deliberate choices that preserve flexibility where it matters. A build-to-suit calls for a different application of the same integrated thinking. With a known user, the focus shifts from preserving optionality to determining how the real estate can best support the company’s operations and long-term objectives. The 65,000-square-foot headquarters project in the same industrial park provides a great example. The company needed a new home base to accommodate its national growth, but the facility also presented an opportunity to address recruitment and retention. In addition to operational and warehouse functions, nearly 20,000 square feet is dedicated to office and employee areas, including a fitness center, locker rooms and a lounge-style break space. In a build-to-suit setting, the value of design-build goes beyond customization. A user may know what they want from a facility without knowing how those priorities translate into square footage, cost or design. When development, design and construction expertise are engaged together, operational needs, workplace goals, budget and schedule can inform one another while decisions are still fluid. The process helps distinguish features that create meaningful value from those that may add cost without advancing the business objective. Start with the business need Integrated thinking can begin even earlier, before a company has determined what form its real estate solution should take. In a market with limited existing inventory, a user may assume that building new is the only alternative. Another may dismiss a build-to-suit because of the perceived time, capital or complexity involved. Neither conclusion should be reached before the options have been tested. Starting with the business requirement rather than a predetermined real estate solution allows an integrated team to evaluate existing buildings, speculative space and build-to-suit opportunities against the same operational, financial and schedule considerations. Early design and construction input can establish what is feasible without requiring a company to advance a full design or commit to a site before it understands the implications. items.title: New Northeast Philly Warehouse Sells For $32M: The Philadelphia Deal Sheet
items.description: A construction materials manufacturer has shelled out $32M for a newly built 103K SF warehouse it will use as a distribution center. Courtesy of Crow Holdings 2748 Grant Ave. Crow Holdings Development sold the 10-acre property across from the Northeast Philadelphia Airport to Spears Manufacturing, which produces plastic pipe fittings and valves. “The rapid sale of 2748 Grant Avenue following delivery, along with the significant interest it generated, underscores pent-up demand for modern, Class A warehouse space in a market where new construction remains limited,” CHD Director Johanna Chervak said in a statement. “For industrial owner-users, finding quality, ‘close-in’ properties available for purchase can be challenging.” The property features 32-foot clear heights, 32 loading dock doors and enough parking for 99 vehicles. A CBRE team including Paul Touhey, Sean Bleiler and James Bolt represented the buyer, while JLL's Jeff Lockard, Larry Maister and Mitch Russell represented the seller. SALES Brennan Investment Group purchased a 100K SF warehouse outside Bethlehem at 47 Commerce Way. The acquisition from the nonprofit Feed the Children came out to $11.5M, according to property records. *** Realterm bought a 7-acre final-mile warehouse and industrial outdoor storage fleet maintenance facility at 461 Harrisport Court in Middletown, south of Harrisburg. It includes a 33K SF warehouse and a 6K SF maintenance shop. Realterm declined to share a sale price. The property was sold to UGI Utilities for $775K in 2022, according to property records. Jennifer Stein of JDS Real Estate Services and an Axiom Capital Advisors team including Jose Sasson-Lerner and Roberto Susi helped facilitate the transaction. *** Courtesy of Post Road Management 303–309 N. 65th St. Post Road Management has acquired two West Philadelphia properties spanning 48 units for a combined $1.35M and plans to renovate both properties. The new additions to its portfolio are 303-309 N. 65th St. and 6522-6526 W. Girard Ave., both of which had been foreclosed on. CONSTRUCTION AND DEVELOPMENT J.G. Petrucci Co. and Mediplex Property Group are working to bring 100K SF of healthcare and retail space to a 15-acre site at 1300 Easton Road in Horsham. Work on the parcel across from the former Willow Grove Naval Air Station is scheduled to begin in the first quarter. *** Shadowbrook Development has received permission from municipal officials in Cinnaminson to build a 45K SF flex warehouse at 2203-2205 Wallace Blvd. The decision was rendered at a meeting Thursday night. PEOPLE Multifamily owner Arden Residential has added two new people to its roster. Brian Collins has joined as president, and Max Spencer has been tapped as managing director of acquisitions and development. THIS AND THAT The Philadelphia Housing Authority and the Philadelphia Building and Construction Trades Council are offering a reward of up to $30K for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the people who shot and injured a PHA employee at the Morton Homes in East Germantown on Saturday. “This was a senseless and cowardly act of violence against a dedicated public servant who comes to work every day to make our communities a better place to live,” PHA CEO Kelvin Jeremiah said in a statement. “An attack on any member of the PHA family is an attack on all of us, and on the residents we serve. We will not tolerate it.” Anyone with information is encouraged to call the Citizens Crime Commission at 215-546-6532 or the PHA Police Department at 215-684-1911. Anonymous tips may be given by calling 215-684-3350 or emailing Phacrimetips@pha.phila.gov . items.title: The Bottom of the Bottom? (November 2026 Housing Market Forecast)
items.description: The Bottom of the Bottom? (November 2026 Housing Market Forecast) Written by Mischa Fisher on November 25, 2026 The shift in strength from the for-sale market to the rental market that we highlighted earlier in the year continues to pick up momentum. The rate of decline has become large enough that Zillow’s latest forecast predicts home sales for full-year 2026 will decline slightly, while home values will have risen only modestly in nominal terms (i.e., home values rising slower than the rate of inflation). Home values are projected to rise 0.4% this year, revised down from 0.7% last month, driven mainly by the run-up in inventory. Mortgage rates hit 7.3% in October and could stay above 7% through mid-2027, which will keep many buyers on the sidelines while listings pile up. Despite new listings slowing year over year, total active listings could be as much as 10% higher than last year by December. Because the labor market is marked by low hiring and low firing, widespread job loss has been avoided, and that has held up best where supply is still tight, in the Central and Northeast regions. The West, with more inventory growth, faces more downward pressure on prices despite the relatively low unemployment rate. Existing home sales are now projected to reach 3.71 million in 2026, down from last month’s estimate of 3.75 million. This means that despite the stronger months during higher-volume portions of the year, the acute slowdown in the lower-volume fourth quarter is putting enough downward pressure on existing home sales that 2026 will finish with slightly fewer home sales than 2025 (but still 2.2% more than 2024). Zillow’s forecast of existing home sales, as measured by NAR, is expected to fall 1.4% to 4.0 million. Zillow projects single-family rents will rise 2.9% in 2026, while multifamily rents are expected to grow 1.8%. The rent forecast was adjusted upward because elevated rates and affordability pressure are pushing more would-be buyers to keep renting. Rent growth is still below historical norms. The Bottom of the bottom? All markets are cyclical, and in time, this too shall pass. But this existing and forecasted acute decline in sales activity, from an already low baseline, does prompt the question: where is the bottom of the bottom? The answer depends in part on which metric we use to define the bottom, and so it is susceptible to shifting with timing, level of aggregation, and seasonal adjustment. For example, Zillow’s existing home sales metric is calculated by counting the complete actuals of sales transactions and comparing those totals to the prior year. This is different method from NAR’s existing sales process, which is based on regional samples and converted into a seasonally adjusted annual rate. Practically, this means the low point of the two methods can differ, and NAR’s could be affected by any drift in regional mix that isn’t picked up by the sampling. But for now, if we define the bottom of the bottom as the peak rate of decline in existing sales from a low baseline level, I think October and November of 2026 have a high likelihood of being the bottom of the post-COVID years. Even though timing the total level of low sales is sensitive to how the trend annualizes, it stands to reason that these months may also represent the lowest total sales volume of the post-COVID era, regardless of whether or not one measures using NAR’s sampled, seasonally adjusted annual rate or Zillow’s full count of transactions. Less volatility, lower inflation, a slowdown in debt issuance to hyperscalers, and the unwinding of some of the global conflicts could all contribute to lower treasuries, lower yield spreads, and higher home sales in the final third of the 2020s. items.title: Court upholds NYC rent freeze backed by Mayor Mamdani
items.description: On Thanksgiving eve, Judge Brendan Lantry dismissed a landlords' challenge to the Rent Guidelines Board's late June decision to freeze rents. The ruling upholds the city's first-ever freeze on both one- and two-year leases. With the national real estate industry watching, the rent freeze became a major test of what a mayor can do to force affordability. Owners of rent-stabilized buildings argued that Mamdani stacked the board with loyalists after promising a freeze, making the outcome predetermined. They also accused the board of following a campaign promise instead of the data on rising landlord costs. Lantry rejected both claims. The ruling comes three weeks after an appeals court revived the city's pied-à-terre tax rollout on second homes valued at $5 million or higher. Mamdani posted on social media that the city has billed owners of those homes more than $500 million. That lawsuit ran parallel to the rent freeze lawsuit landlords filed in late July. It originally was in a Staten Island court but was moved to Manhattan in August at the city's request. The rent freeze took effect Oct. 1 while the lawsuit was pending and covers leases on more than a million apartments. The board had frozen one-year leases in 2015, 2016 and 2020. Because the board acts in a quasi-legislative role, its orders stand if they have a rational basis, and courts may not substitute their own judgment, Lantry wrote. He found that the board's 42-page explanatory statement showed it considered each factor the Administrative Code requires, including the industry's economic condition and the cost of living. Lantry said appointees who share the mayor's views did not show collusion. He noted that "elections have consequences." Ruling comes with criticism But Lantry did not let Mamdani completely off the hook. "Regarding Mayor Mamdani's campaign for Mayor of New York City, the court would be remiss not to state that such comments, promises, and guarantees to freeze the rent were reckless and irresponsible," he wrote. "The Mayor of the City of New York has no authority to unilaterally raise, 'freeze' or otherwise adjust the rent of stabilized units in this City – that responsibility is within the power of the Board and the Board alone." He called an email in which the board's chair shared a draft of the explanatory statement with a mayoral aide before the vote "troubling." He said it cast a "dark shadow" over the board's independence. Without more, he wrote, the email did not justify overturning the decision under Article 78, the state law that lets courts review government agency actions. The judge noted that petitioners agreed to end court-ordered discovery, which produced about 1,000 documents, and never sought depositions. Lantry acknowledged the freeze could make it harder for owners to refinance or renovate. But he wrote that the legal question is not whether the policy is wise. items.description: The Deal Sheet is a weekly compilation of Greater London and beyond's biggest leases, sales, financing deals, construction updates and personnel moves. Have news you'd like to submit? Email mark.faithfull@bisnow.com . BNP Paribas Asset Management Alts and Canadian pension investor PSP Investments are to sell 6 Pancras Square in King's Cross to its occupier, Google, in a £500M deal that will see the investors exit one of their longest-held London office investments. The joint venture acquired the 371K SF, Grade A office building in 2013 through a development forward-funding arrangement, and the property includes 32K SF of retail space across six units. Courtesy of BNPP AM Alts and PSP Investments/Edmund Summer Google is to acquire its headquarters in a deal affirming UK ambitions. BNP Paribas AM Alts, formerly AXA IM Alts, managed the joint venture on behalf of investors including PSP Investments. Google UK and Ireland Managing Director and Vice President Kate Alessi said the purchase underlined the company's long-term commitment to the UK. “Our purchase of 6 Pancras Square sends a clear signal of our long-term commitment to the UK. This investment ensures our UK teams can continue building world-changing AI, driving innovation, and contributing to the growth of the country's economy,” Alessi said in a statement. DEALS London Square has acquired the Boord Street development on Greenwich Peninsula from Fairview New Homes and will deliver all 352 homes as affordable housing through its registered provider, Square Roots. The development has detailed planning permission for three buildings ranging from eight to 25 storeys. The site has been cleared, enabling works have been undertaken, and Building Safety Regulator Gateway 2 approval has been secured, allowing construction to start immediately. Completion is expected in June 2029. The conversion of the previously private-led development into 100% affordable housing has been supported by an £87M grant allocation from the mayor of London. The homes will comprise 80% social rent and 20% intermediate rent, with Greenwich Council making nominations for the social rent properties. *** The Hill Group and Principal Asset Management have agreed a £27.3M transaction for 67 build-to-rent apartments at Canalside Quarter, the first residential phase of the £700M Oxford North master plan. The apartments, comprising one-to-three-bedroom homes, will provide managed rental accommodation within the mixed-use development, which is bringing together residential, research and laboratory space, offices, retail, community facilities and public parks. “This transaction is another important milestone in the growth of Hill's Build-to-Rent platform and demonstrates the increasing confidence institutional investors have in our ability to create high-quality rental homes within thriving mixed-tenure communities,” Hill Senior Asset Manager Tom Starkey said in a statement. *** Savills Investment Management's Simply Affordable Homes fund has acquired 288 affordable homes at Whitstable Heights in Kent from Hyde Housing Association. The purchase, its fourth acquisition, was made through the fund's for-profit registered provider, Simply Affordable Homes RP. The portfolio comprises 204 houses and 84 apartments across social rent, affordable rent and shared ownership tenures and represents the majority of the 400-home development, which was delivered by Hyde in partnership with Chartway Partnerships Group and completed in 2026. The fund now manages more than 700 affordable rent, intermediate rent and shared ownership homes across southern England, the east of England and the Midlands. DEVELOPMENT Developer Hub and Norwegian investor Smedvig have submitted revised plans for the final phase of their One Maidenhead master plan, with proposals for an eight-storey, 70K SF office building. The scheme, named Arven, will sit next to Maidenhead station, between the transport hub and town centre. It will include ground-floor retail and café space, two roof terraces, and additional office and external amenity space. The revised design builds on an existing planning permission, adding a red brick facade to complement the residential buildings and targeting BREEAM Excellent. The first phase of One Maidenhead, completed in 2024, delivered 429 rental homes, 36K SF of retail and restaurant space, and a new public garden. Construction of neighbouring office building Trehus is nearing completion. *** Barratt London and Transport for London property company Places for London have named Ickenham Gardens as the latest site for their West London Partnership joint venture. The site, between Ickenham and Ruislip Gardens, has the potential to deliver around 2,000 homes, half of which would be affordable, alongside improved public green spaces, transport connections and community facilities. The emerging plans will seek to create a new neighbourhood between two established communities, with a mix of home sizes, types and tenures. The proposals also include opportunities for health, education, cultural and community facilities. FINANCE Private credit manager Evermill Capital, backed by Delancey, has launched an infrastructure credit strategy, extending its existing real estate lending platform into infrastructure finance. Evermill has already committed more than £100M to cash-flow-matching infrastructure investments as it develops the new strategy. The business has appointed Tim Floyd as a partner to lead the expansion. He joins from Westbourne Capital, where he spent 13 years building its European infrastructure credit business and deploying more than £3B for insurers, pension funds and sovereign wealth funds. items.title: 725 Houston Apartments Sit Vacant As Fercan Kalkan Fights Foreclosure
items.description: Despite a mounting debt crisis jeopardizing its $1B portfolio, Houston-based multifamily investment firm Kalkan Capital is still clinging to a troubled, 881-unit housing complex following another attempt by its lender to foreclose. Google Maps The entrance to Rockridge Apartments, a mostly vacant apartment complex in North Houston Filings in a Harris County lawsuit show founder Fercan Kalkan objected to an Oct. 7 notice of a foreclosure sale of the property in Houston’s Greenspoint area, arguing the lenders failed to request the court’s permission. The auction, scheduled for earlier this month, didn’t proceed as the legal battle continues, according to court records. Meanwhile, Rockridge Apartments at 16818 City View Place in North Houston sits 82% vacant, and its conditions are allegedly deteriorating as its owner has gone bankrupt and sought to delay a takeover for more than a year. Kalkan, who previously spoke about his aim to revitalize high-crime communities, didn’t respond to a request for comment. An attorney listed as representing his companies in the Harris County lawsuit said he no longer represents Kalkan-related entities and declined to comment further. Rockridge2016 LLC, a Kalkan affiliate, allegedly defaulted on a $54M loan tied to the property in October 2023, according to legal filings. Computershare Trust Co. sued the LLC in February 2025, requesting the appointment of a receiver and the scheduling of a foreclosure sale. That request was granted, but not before Rockridge2016 filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on April 14, 2025, a move that effectively halts foreclosure proceedings. “I think Dr. Kalkan is trying to avoid your honor’s court, if I’m being candid here,” Ross Travis of the Office of the U.S. Trustee said during a September 2025 bankruptcy hearing, according to audio reviewed by Bisnow . “The more that I see of these cases, the more perplexed I am in general,” Travis said. Despite a court-appointed receiver being in place to manage the complex since August 2025, the complex has “numerous units out of service due to roof, electrical, plumbing, foundation, fire or mold issues,” according to a receivership report filed Friday. Only 156 units are occupied, leaving 725 vacant. Occupancy was marginally higher, at 19%, in August as move-outs outpaced move-ins and raids by Immigration and Customs Enforcement at the property were impacting residents, according to special servicer commentary in the Morningstar Credit database. The Rockridge bankruptcy case was dismissed in December 2025 and officially closed in September. It wasn’t the first time Kalkan has averted foreclosure through legal maneuvers and bankruptcy filings . In early October, the same day the lenders filed a public notice for Rockridge Apartments to be sold at a Nov. 3 foreclosure auction, Kalkan filed his objection in the Harris County lawsuit. Attorneys for the lenders responded the next day, saying that as loan guarantor, Kalkan lacks standing to challenge the foreclosure sale and court authorization isn't required to post the sale notice. The latest property records show the last transfer of ownership for the property is still when Rockridge2016 acquired it in 2016. District Court Judge Dawn Rogers hasn't yet acted on any of the October filings. The next hearing in the case is set for Dec. 9. The attorney representing Computershare Trust Co. and LNR Partners , the loan's special servicer, didn't respond to a request for comment. Kalkan-associated LLCs that owned eight Houston-area properties totaling more than 3,000 units faced potential foreclosure in July 2025. At least six of those properties have been transferred to new owners since, according to property records. items.title: Florida Slashed Homestead Taxes. Commercial Real Estate Could Pay The Price
items.description: The Florida commercial real estate industry is holding its collective breath — and hitting pause on some deals — as cities and counties grapple with a new state law that will slash their budgets by millions. Unsplash/Zoshua Colah Miami City Hall at 3500 Pan American Drive Amendment 3, approved on Election Day by 62% of Florida voters, raises the state’s homestead exemption, which only applies to permanent residences, from $50K to $150K next year and $250K in 2028. Set to go into effect by Jan. 1, the law doesn't include tax levies for school district properties. While the new law was passed on the promise of affordability, its impact is prompting local authorities to weigh service reductions, spending freezes, increased fees, and tax rate adjustments that would ultimately leave the private sector to fill the gap. “Our biggest concern, and it applies across the board and all our expenses, is uncertainty,” said Rick Porras, chief financial officer of multifamily developer Neology. “We need to know what playing field we're going to be dealing with.” Gov. Ron DeSantis campaigned on slashing property taxes last year as a way to lower housing costs for homeowners in Florida, where the cost of living index is nearly 2% above the national benchmark, according to a third-quarter Missouri Economic Research and Information Center report . The affordability crisis is more acute in South Florida, where Miami’s cost of living has surpassed that of New York and where more than 50% of Miami-Dade County households are living paycheck to paycheck, the Miami Herald reported . Property taxes account for 43% of municipal general fund revenue, according to a Florida League of Cities study conducted by Wichita State University. Losing a large chunk of that poses a significant risk to local budgets, especially those with smaller commercial real estate tax bases and higher debt levels. Local governments are projected to lose nearly $5B of funding in the next fiscal year, CBS News reported . In response, cities all over the state are canceling Christmas parades , ending funding for transportation services and eyeing hiring freezes and spending cuts . “There are cities that do not have the commercial tax base that would help them offset some of the loss in revenue,” Porras said. “If the cities are heavily dependent on residential properties, they're going to suffer even more than others.” But even cities with a large commercial base are expecting to take a hit, especially to public services. Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins said at Bisnow’s Condoverse conference in April that the city was prepping a 25% budget cut , which would hit city services like local hospitals, police, fire, parks, public schools and water management. Her office didn't respond to a request for comment for this story. Billionaire developer and “ Condo King of Miami ” Jorge Pérez warned such moves could threaten Miami’s ability to attract and retain residents. Some municipalities are considering raising millage rates, or taxing a higher percentage of a property's value. Not only could a higher millage rate cut into the savings homeowners would get with Amendment 3, but commercial owners would face the same higher rate without an exemption to help offset it. Fort Lauderdale Mayor Dean Trantalis told Bisnow the week the amendment passed that he was “very real about raising” his city's millage rates and that he will lean on the community, which will make a decision on “whether they want to increase taxes or reduce services.” “[You] can’t have the same level of service you have come to expect over the years,” he said. “Cities are going to have to deal with it,” he added. “That was a bad choice, but now we have to live with that.” Palm Beach County Administrator Joe Abruzzo told 25 WPBG News in September there were three options for the county to help offset a hit to the budget: cut the budget, significantly affecting first responders and county departments; raise the millage rate; or a combination of both. Assuming there is no taxable value growth, South Florida counties would need to raise their millage rates more than 10% per county to collect the equivalent quantity of tax and keep budgets the same, according to a white paper written by Nick Mau, partner at property tax advisory firm FirstPoint Advisors LLC. A raise in millage rates would likely trickle down to commercial tenants, especially on leases where tenants pay property taxes separately from rent, said Melissa Tapanes Llahues, a land use and zoning attorney and CEO of Bercow Radell Fernandez Larkin and Tapanes. Unsplash/Martley U The Fort Lauderdale skyline While Florida bars municipalities from raising fees on services to generate revenue, a rising concern for the development community is that local governments expand their powers to require greater public improvements and the payment of impact fees, she said. The new law could affect what localities will want developers to build, she added. "I think that government will be more open, welcoming, and incentivize commercial and industrial land uses versus more residential," Tapanes Llahues said. Localities could also shift ad valorem taxes, a challengeable tax based on the assessed value of a property, toward special assessment fees that are based on physical characteristics like square footage or unit count, Mau said. “What we're concerned with is those items being shifted over to the non-ad valorem, and then the property owner has really no way of contesting,” Mau said. DeSantis has tried to take away avenues for localities to raise taxes to compensate for the raised homestead exemption, including passing a law in June that requires a two-thirds vote from local officials to exceed the rollback rate — roughly the same revenue generated from existing properties as the previous year. items.title: Inside a 3-Home Co-Living Compound Designed for Friends To Buy Together
items.description: A co-living community in West Oakland, CA , has hit the market for the first time. The Union is a three-house, 14-bedroom compound and is listed at $2,999,995. That’s the asking price for all three homes. If purchased separately by friends, multigenerational families, or any other buyers who want to live side by side, the starting price is $899,000 for the smallest of the three homes, which has five bedrooms and four bathrooms . Each home is separately deeded as a condo within the greater compound. This lot has been zoned RM-3, or Mixed Housing Type Residential–3, which allows for multiple single-family homes on a single lot. This setup is permissible due to changes in California law allowing for higher-density housing in residential areas. Loading... The Union was built as a three-home, 14-bedroom co-living compound. Aerial Canvas Loading... The design matches the existing look and feel of the neighborhood, which is filled with mostly Victorian homes. Aerial Canvas Loading... The shared rooftop deck boasts views of downtown Oakland. Aerial Canvas This project started in 2019 when a startup called Open Door bought the 7,535-square-foot empty lot and tasked Matt Baran of Baran Studio Architecture with creating a co-living space. They asked: “What if we design something that can be beautiful design and work with the new state laws that allow for increased density in neighborhoods and works well for community living?” says listing agent Max Nelson , who specializes in co-living sales through the platform Live Near Friends . The end result was a rent-by-the-room community where residents enjoyed shared amenities, including a backyard fire pit, co-working space, and rooftop deck with views of downtown Oakland. The design process balanced group-friendly amenities with the look and feel of the neighborhood, which is filled with mostly Victorian homes. Nelson says that the architects asked, “How do we create a modern house without making it look like it doesn't fit?” The design included bay windows that jut from the homes, mirroring the style of a classic Victorian. Having three separate homes rather than one huge building also matched the aesthetic of the area, as did the incorporation of tall, narrow windows. Much of the rest of the design leans more modern, especially the efficient energy systems. The homes rely on shared solar panels, greatly reducing energy bills. Everything is electric—there is no reliance on gas. Each room has its own fan coils to create customized comfort. “It’s a super efficient, well-done system,” says Nelson. Loading... The appliances in the kitchen are electric. Aerial Canvas Loading... The design included bay windows that jut from the homes, mirroring the style of a classic Victorian. Aerial Canvas Because The Union was designed for co-living, some of the best features are the shared spaces and the flow among the three homes. The property fronting the street, 1514, has the smaller price tag at $899,000 and offers 1,919 square feet of living space, including five bedrooms and four bathrooms. A skybridge connects it with the back two condos, positioned side by side like a duplex and sharing a common wall. The larger of the back condos, 1510, is listed at $1,049,500 and sits slightly larger at 2,033 square feet, again with five bedrooms and four bathrooms. Connected is 1512, also offered at $1,049,500 with 2,015 square feet, including four bedrooms and four bathrooms. Above these two condos is the roof area, which houses the solar panels as well as the communal deck with AstroTurf and several seating areas. It all adds up to a highly functional, thoughtfully designed compound that meets the needs of communal living. It offers both shared spaces as well as smaller decks, outdoor seating nooks, and private spaces for solo or one-on-one time with another—because shared living works best when people have the freedom to come together or enjoy time apart. items.description: When John F. Kennedy came home to Hyannis Port for his first Thanksgiving as president, his father still had the best seat in the house. Joseph P. Kennedy presided over the family table, the children ate first, and the cranberries served with dinner came from bogs near the family’s Cape Cod retreat. Five years earlier, it was what happened after Thanksgiving dinner that the family would remember. John, then a Massachusetts senator, slipped into the study off the living room with his father. He had a list of reasons to think twice about running for president. Joseph had an answer for every one. By the time they emerged, the Kennedys had a campaign to plan . Loading... When John F. Kennedy came home to Hyannis Port for his first Thanksgiving as president, his father still had the best seat in the house. Hy Peskin/Getty Images Thanksgiving at the Big House The house where that conversation took place began as a summer rental. In 1926, Joseph and his wife, Rose , brought their children to Malcolm Cottage, a waterfront home overlooking Nantucket Sound. John was just 9. According to the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum, Joseph bought the property two years later for $25,000 and expanded the house to accommodate his growing family. John eventually bought a place of his own behind his parents’ home. His brother Robert and sister-in-law Ethel came to own an adjoining property. Together, the three residences formed the 6-acre compound, an arrangement that put several generations of Kennedys within walking distance of Thanksgiving dinner at the Big House. In "White House by the Sea," author Kate Storey describes a family with surprisingly little use for a formal seating plan. Joseph and Rose took opposite ends of the mahogany table. Everyone else picked a spot. Family cook Ziptha Anderson remembered far less flexibility when it came to carving the bird. “They all like the same thing—the white meat,” she said. The weather had a say in the menu, too. A chilly Thanksgiving called for clam broth, while a mild afternoon meant tomato juice to start. Dinner was at 1 p.m. in Storey’s account of the 1956 gathering, which still left the family time for Mass and a sail before they made their way to the table. A president comes home for the holiday Loading... By Thanksgiving 1961, the guest list included 13 Kennedy adults and 15 Kennedy children. There was room for another family, too. Paul Fay, then undersecretary of the Navy, joined the celebration with his wife and their three children. CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images By Thanksgiving 1961, the guest list included 13 Kennedy adults and 15 Kennedy children. There was room for another family, too. Paul Fay , then undersecretary of the Navy, joined the celebration with his wife and their three children. One family outing took the president and several of his siblings to the skating rink in Hyannis named for their late brother, Joseph Jr. John watched while Ted and his sisters rented skates and played tag on the ice. Back at the compound, Bobby and Ted also got a touch football game going. That evening, the adults sat down to Vermont turkey, candied sweet potatoes, and their choice of pies. Ted found another way to work up an appetite in 1979. A United Press International photographer caught the senator waving from his boat as he took relatives and friends sailing off Hyannis Port before Thanksgiving dinner. Loading... For nearly a century, the Kennedy family's sprawling Hyannis Port compound has served as the backdrop to countless summer celebrations, where days were spent sailing on Nantucket Sound, swimming off the Cape Cod coastline, and taking part in fiercely competitive games of touch football. In 2010, she enlisted her son Robert to bring home two live turkeys so her grandchildren could see the birds up close. One promptly escaped. “For three days they chased it everywhere,” Ethel told the Cape Cod Times. items.title: Denver Multifamily Investors Blame Colorado Regulations For Capital Flight
items.description: Denver’s multifamily market has had an uneven year trying to burn off an oversupply, reduce concessions and stabilize rents. Making the market even more challenging is Colorado legislation, according to panelists at the Nov. 5 Bisnow Multifamily Annual Conference in Denver. Institutional capital has redlined Denver for the past three or four years for a variety of reasons, BMC Investments Chief Investment Officer Matthew Karp said at the event held at The Westin Westminster. “We are big-time on the watch for any global investor right now as a huge political risk, and that is a scary thing when trying to move or [do] development,” Hines Managing Director Elliot Marks said. “Again, that is Denver-specific. Each municipality is different, but the word is out.” Bold Brand/Josh Miles Fairfield & Woods' Ann Chandler, Alpine Investments' Churchill Bunn, Middleburg's Kelly Dranginis, Forum's Chad O'Connor, Vivmark Residential's Todd Nicotra and Hines' Elliot Marks Investors look for business-positive states, and Colorado has implemented less business-friendly policies over the years. This has also impacted the state’s ability to retain and draw new companies and employees, which can directly impact the multifamily market. This year, Colorado has lost 11 public companies and gained two, according to a Nov. 17 report by the Common Sense Institute . A net loss of nine businesses is nearly double the previous record of five losses set in 2019. The last time more public entities moved to Colorado than left was 2022, according to the report. Job growth in the Centennial State has been sluggish this year, too. Colorado’s nonfarm employment trails the national average of 0.6%, growing just 0.3%, or 9,300 jobs , from October 2025 to October 2026. “Job growth is going to be the central factor for what’s going to drive institutional capital,” Karp said. Bold Brand/Josh Miles Bristlecone Construction's Jon Goman, MHK Architecture's Nathan Moore, BMC Investments' Matthew Karp, CBRE's Chris Nebenzahl, Denver Housing Authority's Erin Clark and MGL Partners' Kent Heckaman Denver-based BMC Investment, which decided to pivot away from office and hotel developments to focus solely on multifamily , is “very bullish” on investing in North Carolina because it’s a pro-business environment, Karp said. The company, however, is still trying to invest in the Denver metro, but it can be challenging. “We’re trying to find, at least in Denver, how to be competitive when capital doesn’t necessarily want to be here or [when] they can find better opportunities elsewhere,” Karp said. “Whether it’s regulation, whether it’s taxation, it just becomes more challenging.” Regardless of the recent election , panelists were not optimistic that government regulations will go away or decrease. Bold Brand/Josh Miles Love Wins Leadership's Anissa Faus, Charlesgate's Todd Mikelonis, HED's Otis Odell, Trammell Crow Residential's Daniel Pittenger and Narrate's Adam Fenton “It’s not going to be an overnight panacea,” CBRE Senior Director and Head of Americas Multifamily Research Chris Nebenzahl said. “I think we do still have very, very much an upward hill to climb.” Local advocates and investors believe Denver and the metro have a perception problem that’s making investors and companies question coming to the area. They say changing the narrative will help bring back jobs, people and capital. Denver business leaders are trying to change the city’s perception with a $2.5M campaign called “Denver. The Best Return on Life.” A regional Denver metro campaign called “Yes. And … Colorado” is also trying to change the narrative about doing business along the Front Range. Colorado could “become more attractive” if neighboring business-friendly states turn more regulatory, Alpine Investments Managing Partner Churchill Bunn said at the event. Bold Brand/Josh Miles Renegade Capital's Turner Miller, Prime West Development's Jeff Farmer, Akara Partners' Gregg Christiansen and Embrey's Casey Klein In the meantime, Austin and Denver traded the No. 1 and No. 2 spots for the worst multifamily dynamics in the country, Karp said. An Austin property will trade at 150 to 200 basis points below what it would in Denver. The Austin deal will have a 4% to 4.5% cap rate, but in Denver, the numbers are closer to a mid-5% or 6% cap rate, Karp added. “I don’t know whether or not that’s the right bet or the wrong bet, but that’s how the market is perceived,” Karp said. Bold Brand/Josh Miles QXO's Michael Mazurk, Kephart's Bryce Hall, Nucor Corp.'s Jim Freiberg, JHP Architecture's Sheila Kneifl, Brinkmann Constructors' Jake Snyder and BGRE's Ian Braciszewski “I’d love to see some positive economic activity taking place in terms of companies moving to, growing, staying, whatever the case might be, in Denver, and it’s hard for us to see where that is taking place,” he said. Karp said that when Denver’s job dynamic changes, cap rates will match Austin and other similar cities. Until then, the local multifamily market is in a holding period as the area’s supply gets absorbed. Nebenzahl believes that the local multifamily market will be in for another “soft year” in 2027. He said he’s holding out hope for a “decent recovery” in three to five years. items.title: Challenge To Mamdani's Rent Freeze Thrown Out By Judge
items.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani 's historic rent freeze will stay in place after a judge dismissed a lawsuit Wednesday from a group of landlords. Flickr/Mayoral Photography Office/Ed Reed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani After the New York City Rent Guidelines Board voted in June to freeze rents on one- and two-year leases across the city's 1 million rent-stabilized apartments, landlords represented by Randy Mastro, first deputy mayor under Eric Adams, filed a lawsuit alleging the decision was a result of a “sham process.” But in a decision issued Wednesday morning, New York County Supreme Court Judge Brendan Lantry dismissed the lawsuit, finding that the RGB's decision had “a rational basis,” and therefore the courts had no ability to reverse it. The freeze already went into effect Oct. 1, the first time in the RGB's 57-year history that rents on both one- and two-year leases were barred from being raised. Mamdani campaigned last year on freezing the rent for all four years in office and appointed a majority of the RGB, but the board is supposed to independently make its decision, informed by data, market conditions and public testimony. “When this lawsuit was filed, the Law Department made clear that the board had acted within its authority and that tenants needed this relief,” Mamdani said in a statement. “Today, Judge Lantry affirmed what we knew all along: the Rent Guidelines Board had the authority to deliver for the more than two million New Yorkers who call rent-stabilized apartments home.” A group of landlords that own apartment buildings in Staten Island and Queens, the plaintiffs going after the city, claimed the RGB ignored its own data that showed expenses have skyrocketed for property owners and many were underwater on their mortgages. Some of the landlords are members of the Small Property Owners of New York , which called the dismissal “terribly disappointing.” Owners of rent-stabilized units are dealing with insurance, maintenance and operating costs that have soared in recent years, and they can’t boost their revenue to compensate for higher expenses. “We were hopeful the court would have recognized that the RGB blatantly ignored its own data, which clearly signaled a rent increase, and instead capitulated to the political pressures of City Hall to ensure that Mayor Mamdani made good on his rent freeze campaign promise,” SPONY Board President Ann Korchak said in a statement. “The rent freeze will push more small rent-stabilized property owners to the edge of the cliff.” The landlords allege that Mamdani's administration pressured the RGB into its decision, and they sought to uncover communications between City Hall and board members. More than 1,000 emails and text messages were released as part of the discovery process in the suit, showing frequent outreach from the administration . But after the sides agreed to halt discovery last month, Lantry wrote in his decision that not enough evidence was presented to suggest the city illegally influenced the RGB. But he admonished the new mayor for his campaign vow and the perception it created. “Such comments, promises, and guarantees to freeze the rent were reckless and irresponsible,” the judge wrote. “The Mayor of the City of New York has no authority to unilaterally raise, ‘freeze’ or otherwise adjust the rent of stabilized units in this City — that responsibility is within the power of the Board and the Board alone.” Continue reading this story with a free account Log in or register Related Topics: Ann Korchak , NYC Rent Guidelines Board , Randy Mastro , Rent Freeze , Rent Guidelines Board , Rent Stabilization , Rent stabilized apartments , Small Property Owners of New York , Zohran Mamdani

items.title: Why the Northeast Could Lead a Factory-Built Housing Boom
items.description: Most Americans picture sun-drenched mobile home parks across the South and Southeast when they think of manufactured housing , but more manufactured housing may soon start popping up across the Northeast and West. A new economic research report from Realtor.com® senior economist Joel Berner takes an in-depth look at the manufactured housing guidelines in the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which became law in June. Berner found that cities across the Northeast—including Hartford, CT , Allentown, PA , and Albany, NY —have ideal conditions for a manufactured housing boom: “affordable land, unaffordable traditional new construction, and a low share of single-family starter home inventory.” If you’re not quite sure about what “manufactured housing" means, you’re not alone. For years, people seemingly used “mobile home” and “manufactured housing” interchangeably. But they’re not the same thing. For one, the “mobile home” classification was retired in 1980, though many still use it colloquially. That year, it was replaced by the term “manufactured home.” Broadly, manufactured homes are those built in a factory and then transported to a site. For years, federal Housing and Urban Development code required that all manufactured homes have a permanent steel towing frame underneath. New provisions in the Road to Housing Act, meant to spur more affordable housing, eliminated that requirement. The act further entitles these new chassis-free homes to the same financing, titling, insurance, taxes, transport, and installation as conventional homes. The hope is that creating this new category of manufactured home will help blunt one of the housing industry’s sharpest pain points: affordable starter homes. Loading... In Hartford, CT, starter homes make up just 17.9% of housing inventory, a sign that manufactured housing could have a significant impact on the market. Getty Images Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the number of affordable starter homes for sale has markedly decreased. Realtor.com research found roughly 300,000 fewer affordable “starter” listings on the market today than before the pandemic. The cost of those starter homes rose from $256,000 in 2019 to $344,000 in 2026. By comparison, the median price of a manufactured home in April 2026 was $134,800. To understand what metros might see the biggest impact from this new type of manufactured home, Realtor.com scored the 100 largest metro areas on three metrics: the percentage of single-family starter homes (defined as listings priced at or below 80% of the local median) in the area; the relative price-per-square-foot premiums for traditional new construction; and the availability of affordable vacant land. Loading... The price per square foot for new construction in Albany, NY, is 47% higher than for existing homes. Getty Images Six of the 10 opportunity metros were in the Northeast, including Hartford; Allentown; Albany; Rochester, NY ; Syracuse, NY ; and Worcester, MA . Other metros that made the list were Denver ; Colorado Springs, CO ; Albuquerque, NM ; and Spokane, WA . In Hartford, which ranked first, starter homes account for just 17.9% of single-family inventory, while site-built new construction costs 29.1% more per square foot than existing homes. In third-ranked Allentown, single-family starter homes made up 22.9% of housing in the area, but new-construction costs were 33.6% more than existing homes. In sixth-ranked Albany, starter homes comprised 31.6% of the single-family inventory, but the price per square foot for new construction is 47% higher than for existing homes. That’s nothing compared with seventh-ranked Rochester, where 33.7% of homes are starter but site-built new construction costs 97% more per square foot than existing homes. While the economics in these cities are compelling, another reason manufactured housing may become more popular in these metros is that frigid Northeastern winters limit conventional housing construction. Meanwhile, manufactured housing can be assembled year-round. Before Hartford, Albany, or any other metro can begin taking advantage of the Road to Housing Act’s new manufactured housing rules, municipal zoning laws will need to change, Berner found. According to Land Use Labs data cited in the report, only about 17% of zoned land nationwide explicitly permits manufactured housing communities, and many municipalities enforce minimum floor-size rules or design restrictions that block factory-built units. Julie Gerstein is a writer and editor based in Philadelphia. She previously worked at Business Insider as an executive editor covering news, entertainment, and digital culture, and was the company's founding Singapore bureau chief. She was also a senior editor at BuzzFeed, covering lifestyle, fashion, and beauty. She earned a B.A. in women's studies from the University of Pennsylvania and an M.A. in media and cultural studies from the University of Sussex.

items.description: An Oregon family transformed a mobile home that had sat abandoned for nearly five years into a home for a loved one–all without paying a dime for the property itself . But getting the home for free was only the beginning. recent_coverage.summary_zh: 江森自控整租了圣安东尼奥附近得州舍尔茨一座 53.6 万平方英尺的仓库，业主为 Core5 Industrial Partners，戴德梁行代表业主完成租赁。

recent_coverage.title: Equus Acquires 420,643 SF Logistics Center in Wilmer, Texas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Equus 关联公司通过合资收购达拉斯以南威尔默一座 420643 平方英尺的配送中心。该物业建于 2024 年，成交时已全部出租。

recent_coverage.title: Bank earnings dip as unrealized losses rise by 48% in Q3
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国银行业 2026 年第 3 季度盈利 848 亿美元，环比下降、同比上升；证券未实现亏损同比扩大，贷款余额同比增长 7.5%，国内存款连续 9 个季度增加。

recent_coverage.title: Irvine Retail Center Sells for $31.4M
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据报道，一名私人投资者以 3140 万美元购入尔湾一座 32,560 平方英尺的零售中心。项目由 2 栋建筑组成，设有传统零售铺位及室内外美食广场。

recent_coverage.title: Number of High-Intent Home Shoppers Dropped to a New Low Last Quarter as Stubborn Mortgage Rates Stymied Demand
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zillow 称，2026 年第三季度，美国每套待售挂牌房源平均有 3.5 名收藏或分享房源的用户，同比下降 4.8%，为该指标 2023 年开始跟踪以来最低。规模最大的 50 个大都会区中，44 个同比下降；Zillow 认为，按揭成本上升最可能是需求走弱的主因。

recent_coverage.title: Flat Conditions for Built-to-Rent Construction
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 根据 Census 数据估计，2026 年第三季度单户 BTR 开工约 19,000 套，同比增加 6%；最近四个季度开工 69,000 套，与此前四个季度持平。统计仅涵盖建商自持出租的住宅，不包括售予第三方出租的住宅。NAHB 指出，随后颁布的法律未纳入其认为会损害 BTR 的融资条款。

recent_coverage.title: $500M Data Center Debt Auction Fizzles, Leaving Dutch Bank To Shop For Buyers
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bisnow 援引彭博报道称，因买方需求疲弱，ING 放弃对 5 亿美元数据中心债务的竞价流程，转为寻求逐笔成交。其中，为 Project Jupiter 提供融资的 2,500 万美元债务报价过低；汇丰另以每 1 美元面值不足 90 美分的价格出售了 3 亿美元该项目的建设债务。

recent_coverage.title: Washington state regulator issues temporary stop on new business for Directors Mortgage
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 华盛顿州金融机构部（DFI）因检查受阻及对公司财务状况的担忧，暂令 Directors Mortgage 停止承接州内新业务，包括向该州居民发放贷款或为位于该州的房产发放贷款。监管机构要求该公司提交财务资料、完整回应传票并履行未清偿的财务义务。

recent_coverage.title: The Geography of the Crowded Nest: Where Adults Are Living with Their Parents
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com Research 称，2025 年美国有 2,520 万名 18--34 岁成年人和父母同住，人数创纪录，占同龄人群的 33.0%，仍低于 2020 年创下的 33.6%。东北部比例为 36.9%，居各地区之首；纽约大都会区以 41.3% 居主要大都会区首位。

recent_coverage.title: Stability concerns have Fed considering dormant capital rule
recent_coverage.summary_zh: National Mortgage News 称，部分美联储官员讨论启用逆周期资本缓冲，以应对金融稳定风险；该工具会在经济上行期提高银行资本，但目前仍是讨论。

recent_coverage.title: Mount Street Establishes New Dallas Hub, Buys $1.4B Servicing Business
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Mount Street Group 在达拉斯组建新团队，并收购 Goldersun 的贷款服务组合，为其规模约 300 亿美元的美国贷款服务组合新增近 14 亿美元的服务规模。新团队将负责美国证券化产品、CLO 及特殊贷款服务业务。

recent_coverage.title: FHA’s reverse mortgage book faces headwinds from home prices, fewer payoffs
recent_coverage.summary_zh: FHA 精算报告显示，从 2025 财年到 2026 财年，MMI 基金总体资本比率由 11.47% 降至 10.29%，仍高于 2% 的法定最低要求；HECM 逆向抵押贷款组合的资本比率由 24.06% 降至 5.43%。该组合仍盈利，占基金有效在保规模不到 4%。房价涨幅放缓和宏观预测更新推高了预计损失，贷款结清减

recent_coverage.title: New York Governor signs new rules for private listings into law, Compass praises it
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 纽约州新法要求住宅挂牌在公众无需付费、也无需与指定经纪机构或经纪人合作即可查阅的平台上公开营销。卖方签署州统一披露表并确认知悉非公开营销的风险与取舍后，可以不公开营销，但不得通过大众营销渠道将挂牌信息传播至挂牌经纪人所属机构之外。

recent_coverage.title: Gilbane, Florida Polytechnic University to Break Ground on Residence Hall, Dining Facility
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 佛州理工大学与 Gilbane 的合作项目包括 601 床位宿舍及餐饮设施，预计 2027 年春季开工、2028 年秋季完工，项目通过免税债券融资。

recent_coverage.title: CenterSquare sells Kennesaw multifamily community
recent_coverage.summary_zh: CenterSquare 出售位于 Kennesaw、拥有 240 套公寓的 Mill at Chastain 社区。交易方未披露财务细节；Cobb County 税务记录显示，该物业最近一次过户价格约为 4,260 万美元。CenterSquare 称，其以 core-plus 策略升级了部分单元，65% 的单元未做

recent_coverage.title: Mountain View Hotel Refinanced with New Loan for $77M
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Broadreach 为 Mountain View 的 255 间客房 Ameswell Hotel 获得 $77M 浮动利率再融资贷款，由 Brookfield 提供资金，JLL Capital Markets 安排。

recent_coverage.title: Martin Commercial Properties Lands $15M in Construction Money for Phoenix Development
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Martin Commercial Properties 获得 $15M 五年期建设贷款，用于凤凰城 102,302 平方英尺 Class A 灵活工业项目；贷款含 36 个月只付息期，支持施工及租赁爬坡。

recent_coverage.title: Chicago multifamily sales activity nears decade high
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，芝加哥多户住宅年内交付超过 3,800 套，第三季度空置率上升 10 个基点至 5.6%。挂牌月租金为 2,047 美元，环比持平、同比上涨 2.3%；第三季度销售活动加快。

recent_coverage.title: Single-Family Home Size Rising
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 称，2026 年第三季度新建单户住宅平均面积为 2,455 平方英尺，同比小幅增加；中位数为 2,164 平方英尺，较前一季度略降。NAHB 认为，高端市场相对强劲，但住房可负担性仍将限制面积增幅。

recent_coverage.title: REIT Sells 400-Unit Arlandria Apartment Community For $69M
recent_coverage.summary_zh: UDR 将自 2002 年持有的花园式公寓社区 Presidential Greens 以 6,900 万美元售予 Blackfin 与 JSB 的合资企业。该社区位于弗吉尼亚州北部，共有 396 套住宅。买方认为，物业受益于华盛顿特区都会区多户交付放缓、可负担住房需求及靠近就业中心的区位。

recent_coverage.title: What's driving seller confidence in 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Century 21 Real Estate 委托 Ipsos 开展的调查显示，计划在 12 个月内出售住房的业主中，75% 认为现在适合搬家；已挂牌业主中，这一比例为 82%。86% 的受访卖方称，自己的按揭利率至少在一定程度上影响了搬家时点。

recent_coverage.title: JLL Arranges Loan for Refinancing of Mixed-Use Portfolio in Fort Worth
recent_coverage.summary_zh: JLL 代表借款人 Magnolia Equity Partners，经一家未具名的人寿保险公司，为 Fort Worth 两栋混合用途建筑安排五年期固定利率再融资贷款，贷款金额未披露。

recent_coverage.title: Garden Communities Progresses with West Hartford Multifamily Development
recent_coverage.summary_zh: The Residences at Heritage Park 将提供 322 套豪华出租公寓，项目施工正在推进，预计 2027 年晚春开业；开发商称其位于当地活跃且需求旺盛的住房市场。

recent_coverage.title: Mortgage Rates Much Lower on Friday
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 10 年期美债收益率日内下行超过 0.13%，30 年期固定按揭利率指数降至 7.33%，较前一日下降 0.12%，为 11 月 10 日以来最低。

recent_coverage.title: Kansas City BTR construction has declined from 2023 peak
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，堪萨斯城 BTR 过去 3 个月空置率下降 30 个基点至 8.1%，要价租金同比上涨 3% 至每月 $ 2,153；今年计划交付约 500 套。

recent_coverage.title: Dallas-Fort Worth multifamily rents post first annual gain in three years
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 数据显示，达拉斯--沃思堡第三季度净吸纳约 6,600 套，略超 6,400 套新增供应；空置率降至 6.0%，租金同比上涨 0.5%，为 2023 年第三季度以来首次年度上涨。

recent_coverage.title: U.S. concession use falls again, but the depth of discount is the deepest in 15 years
recent_coverage.summary_zh: RealPage 称，美国公寓让利使用率 10 月连续第 5 个月下降至 13.1%，但平均折扣升至 11.2%，为 2010 年 1 月以来最深，约相当于 12 个月租约免租 5.8 周。

recent_coverage.title: New Home Market Update
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zonda 研究显示，10 月新房销售环比下降 3.1%、同比下降 11.7%；86% 建商称需求低于预期，购房者流量和紧迫感走弱，激励措施对利润率的压力仍在。

recent_coverage.title: Texas Housing Insight | November 2026 | Texas Real Estate Research Center
recent_coverage.summary_zh: TRERC 称，德州 9 月成屋销售同比下降，房价基本持平；按揭利率、通胀与可负担性约束需求，库存仍接近夏季峰值，市场预计年末仍偏弱。

recent_coverage.title: AI Wealth Is Raising Down Payments in the Bay Area, and Beyond
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com Research 称，旧金山、圣马特奥和圣克拉拉首付中位数由 2020--2022 年的 20.4% 升至 2024--2026 年的 25%；AI 相关高收入需求也与湾区租金快速上涨一致。

recent_coverage.title: Everyday Economics: The federal government delayed the housing recovery – The Center Square
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 文章援引 NAR 称，10 月成屋销售季调年率降至 375 万套，同比下降 8.8%，为 2010 年 8 月以来最低；按揭成本上升继续压制可负担性。

recent_coverage.title: Housing groups cheer Senate passage of milestone permitting bill
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 美国参议院以 62-33 票通过 BAAJA，法案拟简化住房等项目联邦许可、降低开发成本；现提交众议院，能否在新国会前完成仍待观察。

recent_coverage.title: Formation Breaks Ground On 673K SF Industrial Park: The Houston Deal Sheet
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Formation Interests 与 Ares Management 合作，在休斯顿 Spring 开发 673K SF 工业园，含 6 栋楼和配套设施，预计 2027 年底完工。

recent_coverage.title: How Much of a Pay Raise Would Today’s Renters Need to Afford a Home? – MortgagePoint
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NRHC 文章称，全国单户出租屋典型月租为 $ 2,243，而 20% 首付购房月成本为 $ 2,603；按 30% 收入规则，购房所需年收入为 $ 104,132，高于租房的 $ 89,724。

recent_coverage.title: Ascendant Capital Partners Acquiring the Westin Seattle Hotel
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Ascendant Capital Partners 将收购西雅图 891 间客房的 Westin Seattle，HEI Hotels and Resorts 计划自 2027 年 1 月 26 日接管运营。

recent_coverage.title: Atlanta multifamily sales accelerate in the third quarter
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Northmarq 称，亚特兰大第三季度吸纳近 3,900 套、超过交付约 800 套，空置率降至 5.7%，租金同比上涨 1.3%；截至 9 月交易数量同比增 20%。

recent_coverage.title: Vacant Since 2012 Fire, East Flatbush Site Will Yield 134 New Apartments
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 布鲁克林 East Flatbush 项目已开工，将在 2028 年完工后提供 134 套住房，其中 90 套为可负担住房；项目使用市级循环贷款工具。

recent_coverage.title: Closings decrease 21% in Houston
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 休斯顿截至 11 月 16 日当周成交量同比下降 21% 至 1,115 套，住宅签约量下降 25.3% 至 1,477 套；新挂牌量同比下降 2.3%，市场活动整体走弱。

recent_coverage.title: FPA Multifamily Picks Up 599-Unit MF Community in Portland
recent_coverage.summary_zh: FPA Multifamily 已购入波特兰 599 套 Wimbledon Square and Gardens，社区建于 1973 年和 1975 年，含公寓与联排住宅及多项配套。

recent_coverage.title: Top 10 U.S. Metros Leading the Annual Growth in Purchase Mortgage Originations
recent_coverage.summary_zh: ATTOM 称，2026 年第三季度住宅按揭发放总量为 1.29 million 笔，环比下降 12%、同比下降 15%；购房贷款 729,968 笔，为 2012 年以来第三季度最低。

recent_coverage.title: Bascom Group Acquires 370-Unit Workforce Housing Property in North Dallas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bascom Group 收购北达拉斯 370 套工薪住房，并通过 MORE Capital 获得收购融资；公司计划进行资本改造，Northmarq 负责经纪与融资安排。

recent_coverage.title: Weekly Housing Trends: U.S. Market Update (Week Ending Nov. 14, 2026)
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com Research 周度数据称，截至 11 月 14 日，活跃库存同比增 8.6%，但住宅签约量 10 月环比下降 4.7%、同比下降 16.7%，中位挂牌价同比下降 2.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Machine Investment Group Buys 490-Unit Apartment Community in North Dallas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Machine Investment Group 与 RPM Living 收购北达拉斯 490 套 75 West，项目含 10,800 平方英尺零售空间；交易通过贷款方主导的场外流程完成，RPM Living 将负责管理。
